name: pixel-heading-character
title: Pixel Heading
description: A large display heading where each character is set in a different pixel font, the mix stepping through its faces on a timer so the word ripples and re-forms in new lettering.
use: A short display headline should feel lo-fi and animated, with the type itself carrying the personality.
avoid: It needs five pixel web fonts registered, and the lettering only works at display size; body copy becomes hard to read.
a11y: The heading exposes its full text while each letter span is hidden, and Enter or Space advances it; motion ignores prefers-reduced-motion. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A wide white heading on near-black, its glyphs built from dots, tiny squares and thin strokes so neighbouring letters look like different typefaces. Underneath sits a small uppercase label naming the current mode.
behaves: Left alone in auto-play it keeps stepping each character to the next font on its own delay, so the change travels across the word like a ripple. Hovering or focusing restarts the cascade, and each letter is a separate span swapping a font class.
customise: Pass the heading as children and choose mode, cycleInterval, staggerDelay, autoPlay and showLabel, plus a static prefix and an isolate map. The five faces are CSS classes.
weight: light: A line of spans and one timer that only changes class names.
